According to a report by 404 Media, digital forensics company Magnet Forensics stated that its products have found a way to bypass a security feature on the iPhone. This feature automatically restarts the device after it remains locked for 72 consecutive hours. Details are as follows.

Some background information

Nearly two years ago, the iOS 18.1 update introduced the "Inactivity Reboot" feature, which forces an iPhone to restart after it remains locked for 72 consecutive hours.

The core purpose of this feature is to make it more difficult for law enforcement agencies and forensic tools to access data on a locked iPhone, as after a restart the device returns to the "Before First Unlock" (BFU) state, rather than remaining in the less restrictive "After First Unlock" (AFU) state.

When an iPhone is in the BFU state, some sensitive data remains protected by encryption keys. These keys only become active after the user enters the passcode for the first time, at which point the device enters the AFU state.

After entering the AFU state, more data on the device can be accessed until the next restart; once it restarts again, the device returns to the BFU state.

The iPhone's automatic restart means that even if law enforcement seizes a device, it may revert to the BFU state before investigators can access it, because obtaining a search warrant or transporting the device to a forensic lab takes time.

When iOS 18.1 was released, 404 Media pointed out that this feature would also make it harder for thieves or other bad actors to keep a stolen iPhone in the AFU state for extended periods, thereby developing or using methods to crack it.

GrayKey reportedly already able to bypass "Inactivity Reboot"

404 Media reported today that, based on a "training and demonstration video produced for law enforcement that appears to have been filmed in early 2025," Magnet Forensics, the developer of the GrayKey phone-unlocking tool, appears to have developed a way to bypass the iPhone's "Inactivity Reboot" feature.

The report states that Magnet has developed a new device called GrayKey Preserve, and has also added an "Evidence Preservation Mode" to its existing GrayKey hardware.

Both are designed to maintain the iPhone's forensic state while avoiding immediate exposure of the data stored on the device, allowing law enforcement officers to keep that state unchanged while awaiting search authorisation.

The report noted that although the video did not explain in detail the technical principles of the bypass mechanism, it stated that even if the iPhone restarts, GrayKey can still keep it in the AFU state.

The report states:

404 Media reached out separately to Apple and Magnet Forensics, and neither responded to requests for comment. They also consulted iPhone security researcher Jiska Classen, who said Magnet may have found a way to tamper with the iPhone's system clock, or to disable the processes responsible for invalidating certain data.

Although the video appears to have been filmed in early 2025, it remains unclear how long this technology has been available to law enforcement agencies, whether it has been used in actual investigations, and whether it still works against the latest version of iOS.
